rationale: Fire and smoke damage to the claimant's own kitchen cabinets, ceiling, and walls caused by an accidental grease fire—a direct loss to the claimant's property covered under property damage.
claim_summary: Policy POL-1001 (Alex Doe, homeowners, active): Grease fire in kitchen caused by sauteing incident yesterday evening. Claimant extinguished fire with fire extinguisher. Damage includes charred kitchen cabinets above stove and smoke damage to ceiling and walls. No injuries. Deductible $500, coverage limit $250,000. Classified as property_damage with 0.95 confidence. Severity: medium—moderate loss to kitchen surfaces contained to one room with no injuries or rest-of-home damage.

case_facts.description: fire on stove from grease flare-up while sauteing onions, extinguished with fire extinguisher
case_facts.damage_type: charred kitchen cabinets above stove and smoke damage on ceiling and walls

rationale: Water damage from the claimant's own plumbing system to their own property (hardwood flooring, drywall, and stored belongings) is direct property damage covered under homeowners insurance.
claim_summary: Policyholder: Sam Patel (POL-1004, homeowners premium, active). Incident: Basement flooding due to burst/failed plumbing in claimant's home. Damage: Approximately 2 inches of water across entire basement, buckled hardwood flooring, drywall soaked up to 1 foot, and ruined stored boxes discovered upon return from work trip. Classification: Property damage (confidence 0.95). Severity: High. Coverage limit: $750,000; deductible: $500. Requires immediate water mitigation and assessment of structural damage and personal property loss.

rationale: Wind damage to the claimant's own roof shingles is straightforward property damage to the claimant's home.
